title: A loop with a decision inside — gently
idea: A quick peek: the loop body can be any step you know, including an if. The body still just repeats each pass. Reviews if from earlier laps.

exercises.prompt: Can the body of a 'for each' loop contain an if?
options: Yes — the body can be any steps you know, including an if
exercises.explanation: The body is just steps; an if is a step. Each pass runs the if again. We'll go deeper later — this is a gentle peek.

exercises.prompt: Review: what does an if do?
options: Runs its indented step only when the condition is true
exercises.explanation: if is a yes/no gate: the body runs only when the condition is true. A loop, by contrast, repeats.

exercises.prompt: A loop repeats, and an if decides — they do different jobs.
exercises.explanation: Loop = repeat; if = choose. They combine well: repeat a check for each pass. Different tools, different jobs.
7 is greater than 3, so 7 > 3 is True. Comparisons feed if conditions — a quick recap from Lap 2.

exercises.prompt: In 'for each pass: if ...: print(...)', how many times does the if get checked over 4 passes?
exercises.explanation: The whole body repeats each pass, so the if runs once per pass — four checks over four passes.

exercises.prompt: Each pass of a loop runs the whole body fresh, including any if inside it.
exercises.explanation: Yes — every pass re-runs the body top to bottom. An if inside gets re-evaluated each time.

exercises.prompt: Match each tool to its one-line job.

pairs.right: Do a step only when true

exercises.explanation: You now have repeat, decide, and show — the building blocks you'll combine in later units.

exercises.prompt: Why only a gentle peek at if-inside-a-loop now?
options: Combining them fully comes in a later unit; first get the loop shape solid
Because if does not work in loops
exercises.explanation: One idea at a time: solid loops first, then combining with if later. For now, just know the body can hold any step.

exercises.prompt: Review: = and == are different. Which one COMPARES two values?
exercises.explanation: == compares; = assigns. A recap from Lap 2 that stays true inside loops too.

exercises.prompt: The big takeaway of this unit so far?
options: A 'for each' loop repeats a body once per thing, and the body can be any steps
exercises.explanation: The loop repeats a body per item; the body is ordinary steps. That foundation carries into for + range next.
